title: Derived sections on a flat face total site and their augmentation
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $a:W_\bullet\to Z$ be an augmented semisimplicial algebraic space: it is indexed contravariantly by the nonempty finite ordinals and injective order-preserving maps. Suppose every face map and every $a_p:W_p\to Z$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] on etale scheme charts. Use enlarged small etale ringed sites [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] and their ringed total module category $\mathscr M$ and augmentation $a$ [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Let $F\in\mathscr M$ be any module, and choose a bounded-below injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathscr M$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every etale algebraic space $V\to Z$, put $V_p=W_p\times_ZV$. There is a natural isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$R\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{et}},(Ra_*F)|_V)\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Tot}(A_V),\qquad A_V^{p,q}=\Gamma((V_p)_{\mathrm{et}},I_p^q|_{V_p}),\quad p,q\ge0.$$
Here $(I_p^q)$ is component evaluation, the horizontal differential is $\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^i d_i^*$ using the semilinear transition of $I^q$ and adjunction, and the total differential is $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The $p$-th column represents $R\Gamma((V_p)_{\mathrm{et}},F_p|_{V_p})$. The construction is invariant under face-compatible zigzags of column quasi-isomorphisms between resolution diagrams with one common lower bound on the internal degree; the totalization is taken after choosing such compatible resolution diagrams, not from an isolated family of cohomology groups. For $F=a^*G$, with $G$ a module on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, these identifications respect the augmentation: the map induced by the canonical derived adjunction unit $\eta_G:G\to Ra_*a^*G$ is represented by the augmented restriction map from a resolution model of $R\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{et}},G|_V)$ to the displayed total complex, and this remains true after such replacements. A map between bounded-below derived modules on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an isomorphism if its derived sections on every etale $V\to Z$ are isomorphisms. Neither a hypercover condition nor quasi-coherence of $F$ or $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work on the enlarged sites, so that an etale algebraic space $V\to Z$ is an object and its slice is the site of $V$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison] chartwise flatness of each face and $a_p$ is ringed-topos flatness. In the equivalent scalar-extension formulation [def-sfb-flat-etale-ringed-map], extension of scalars is exact. Transport of modules by inverse image is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]; their composite, module pullback, is therefore exact. Every transition $f_\alpha$ is a composite of faces, so by the composition compatibility of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] its module pullback is a composite of these exact face pullbacks, hence exact, as the free-adjoint node requires. Evaluations are exact and jointly conservative by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category], so $a^*$ is exact as well: evaluate the cohomology of the image of a short exact sequence, obtaining the zero cohomology of each $a_p^*$ image. The exact left adjoint $\ell_p$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] and [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] show that $I_p^q=e_pI^q$ is injective; the same adjoint argument for $a^*\dashv a_*$ shows that $a_*I^q$ is injective. Exact evaluation makes $F_p\to I_p^\bullet$ a resolution. All module categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], including the module category of the total ring sheaf.

source.place: Tags 0D72 and 0D74 (component extension); 0D7B (flat augmentation). Flatness comparison uses the cited algebraic-space node; 04JC, sites-modules-lemma-flat-pullback-exact.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary base module $H$, put $P_p(H)=\ell_p(a_p^*H)$. The component formula in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] and the augmentation composition identifications in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] give
$$(P_p(H))_m=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\hookrightarrow[m]}a_m^*H.$$
Define $d_i:P_p(H)\to P_{p-1}(H)$ on the $\alpha$ summand by the identity into the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand, and $P_0(H)\to a^*H$ by folding summands. Postcomposition of labels commutes with deletion, and the pullback composition identifications obey the cocycle law, so these are maps of systems. Double deletion cancels in pairs with opposite signs; thus the alternating boundary squares to zero. In component $m$ this augmented chain complex is contractible. Write a summand as an increasing tuple $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$. Let $h$ insert $0$ at the start if $i_0>0$, and be zero if $i_0=0$; let $h_{-1}$ send the augmented term to the vertex $0$. If $i_0>0$, the first face of $(0,i_0,\ldots,i_p)$ is the original tuple, and all other faces cancel the terms of $h\partial$. If $i_0=0$, only its first face has nonzero $h$ and gives the original tuple. Hence $\partial h+h\partial=1$, including augmentation degree $-1$. This also covers $m=0$ and the zero terms $p>m$. Consequently $P_\bullet(H)\to a^*H$ is exact, since exact jointly conservative evaluations detect its cohomology. The contractions need not commute with $m$; only the differentials must be maps of systems.

source.place: Tag 0D7C, lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules; agent adaptation to injective labels: finite ordered simplex, with its contraction written here.

proof.text:
For an injective total module $J$, apply $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr M}(-,J)$ to the exact augmented resolution in Step 2. Injectivity makes the resulting cochain complex exact: a map annihilating a boundary factors through its image quotient and extends across the next monomorphism. The free adjunction and $a_p^*\dashv a_{p,*}$ identify its terms with $\operatorname{Hom}(H,a_{p,*}J_p)$, and its augmented term with $\operatorname{Hom}(H,a_*J)$. Under the explicit inverse-adjunct formula the $i$th coface is the transpose of the transition along $\delta_i$, with sign $(-1)^i$; the augmentation is the transpose of the component of $a^*a_*J\to J$. Now take $H=E_V$, the free representable module of [lem-trf-free-representable-module-ext-evaluation]. Its displayed evaluation bijection turns this exact sequence into
$$0\to\Gamma(V,a_*J)\to\Gamma(V_0,J_0)\to\Gamma(V_1,J_1)\to\cdots.$$
Here $a_{p,*}J_p$ evaluated at $V$ is $J_p(W_p\times_ZV)$ by the fibre-product description of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Thus exactness holds on these sections, rather than merely as sheaves. It is natural in $J$ and $V$: a restriction carries a section to its restriction, and on free generators the corresponding map sends $e_{\mathrm{id}}$ to the generator of the site arrow, so the adjunction bijections commute with it.

source.place: Tag 0D7D, lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules; Hom proof applied to the face-only exact complex of Step 2.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to every $J=I^q$. Naturality in $J$ makes all cofaces commute with $d_I$, and the face identities already checked give $d_h^2=0$. Therefore the groups $A_V^{p,q}$ in the statement form a first-quadrant double complex, with total differential $d_h+(-1)^pd_I$. Put $B_V^q=\Gamma(V,a_*I^q)$. The row augmentations define $b_V:B_V\to\operatorname{Tot}(A_V)$ by inclusion into bidegree $(0,q)$; the first horizontal differential kills that augmentation, so this is a chain map. Regard $B_V$ as a double complex concentrated in horizontal degree zero. On horizontal cohomology, Step 3 says $b_V$ is the identity identification in degree zero and both sides vanish in positive horizontal degrees. Apply the horizontal-first spectral sequence and functorial finite-filtration convergence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. The induced maps on $E_1$ and hence on every associated graded of total cohomology are isomorphisms. Successive short exact sequences of the finite filtrations then show $H^n(b_V)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. Thus $b_V$ is a quasi-isomorphism of entire complexes.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules, double-complex proof; Homology Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, second-variable variant.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], $a_*I^\bullet$ represents $Ra_*F$. By Step 1 it is a bounded-below complex of injectives, and so are all $I_p^\bullet$. They are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Slice restriction preserves K-injectivity by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Consequently $B_V$ represents $R\Gamma(V,(Ra_*F)|_V)$ and each column $A_V^{p,\bullet}$ represents $R\Gamma(V_p,F_p|_{V_p})$. The slice identifications are those of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Combined with $b_V$, this gives the asserted derived isomorphism, including the horizontal maps, since Step 3 identified their actual adjoints. If the derived sections are read as sections of underlying abelian complexes, [lem-sfb-ringed-sections-forget-abelian] supplies precisely the same comparison, naturally with all restriction maps. No claim that forgetting modules preserves injectivity is needed. Naturality of $b_V$ and of the canonical resolution comparisons gives naturality in $F$ and $V$.

For a face-compatible column quasi-isomorphism $A\to A'$ of section resolution diagrams, shift a common internal lower bound $c$ to zero and apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison]. The shifted total has the same horizontal signs, and its vertical differential agrees with the shift of the original total after multiplying the horizontal-degree-$p$ summand by $(-1)^{cp}$; indeed this changes the horizontal sign by $(-1)^c$ and leaves the vertical sign unchanged. Thus the comparison also holds before shifting. Each arrow of a zigzag therefore gives an isomorphism of total derived objects; invert arrows pointing backwards. Compatibility of entire diagrams is used here to obtain double-complex maps, and the common lower bound makes each total diagonal finite. For two total injective resolutions of $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives their comparison under $F$, unique up to homotopy; evaluation and sections carry that homotopy to column homotopies, and its total is the homotopy with sign $(-1)^p$ on horizontal degree $p$. Thus the construction is independent of this choice as well. This proves the stated invariance without replacing the compatible diagram by its separate cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 0133, homology-lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution and column-cone comparison; agent sign and common-lower-bound verification.

proof.text: Take $F=a^*G$ and a nonnegative injective resolution $G\to J^\bullet$ on the base. Exactness of $a^*$ makes $a^*G\to a^*J$ a quasi-isomorphism. Since $I$ is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents its derived inverse followed by $a^*G\to I$ by a chain map $t:a^*J\to I$, compatible with $G$ in the homotopy category. Termwise adjunction gives $t^\flat:J\to a_*I$. To check the derived adjunction rather than choose an unrelated map, use [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]: it is the adjunction obtained by deriving this ordinary adjunction. Its hypotheses hold: $\mathscr M$ and the base module category are Grothendieck (Step 1), so every unbounded complex has a K-injective resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]; by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] such a resolution $K\to I_K$ receives a unique homotopy class from every quasi-isomorphic $K'$ under $K$, so the ind-system defining $Ra_*K$ is essentially constant with value $a_*I_K$; and $a^*$ is exact, so the pro-system defining $La^*$ at $M$ is essentially constant with value $a^*M$. Its Hom bijection on these representatives is the termwise bijection, since exact $a^*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and maps into K-injective $I$ are computed in the homotopy category. The adjunct of $t$ is therefore the unit $G\to Ra_*a^*G$, as $t$ represents the identity of $a^*G$. On sections its composite with $b_V$ is the map $\Gamma(V,J)\to A_V^{0,\bullet}\to\operatorname{Tot}(A_V)$ obtained from the degree-zero component $t_0$ and the augmentation adjunction; the first face difference is zero by compatibility of $t$ with the two transitions. This is exactly the augmented restriction map. A map of augmented resolution diagrams commutes with these maps before localization; Step 6 inverts its total quasi-isomorphism. Hence the same unit identification survives all the stated compatible replacements.

source.place: Tag 0D7D augmentation normalization; derived.tex lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; agent verification for the actual canonical unit.

proof.text: Finally let $u:K\to L$ be a map of bounded-below derived modules whose derived sections on every etale $V\to Z$ are isomorphisms. Represent $K,L$ by bounded-below injective complexes using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], and represent $u$ by a chain map using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Slice K-injectivity [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] says that its section maps compute the assumed derived-section maps. Thus for every object $V$ the cone of that section map is acyclic. Form the cone complex of presheaves of modules by forgetting the sheaf condition. Its evaluation is that same cone (cones use only finite sums), so its cohomology presheaves vanish objectwise. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] now makes its sheafified cone acyclic; sheafifying the original sheaf terms gives them back, so this is the cone of $u$ in module sheaves. Therefore $u$ is an isomorphism in the derived category. The enlarged site covers every algebraic-space etale object and contains all scheme etale objects, by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. This proves the asserted detection. The argument used neither hypercover exactness nor quasi-coherence: horizontal exactness came from injectivity on the total category, not from descent of $F$.
